title: Is Factuality Enhancement a Free Lunch For LLMs? Better Factuality Can Lead to Worse Context-Faithfulness

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of this contribution is to determine whether popular LLM factuality-enhancement methods actually improve factual accuracy and how reliably. None of the prior papers explicitly report or establish this same empirical relationship. While several papers address related topics (e.g., [5], [6], [8], [9], [13], [11]), they focus on proposing or evaluating methods for mitigating hallucinations or improving truthfulness, rather than systematically assessing the reliability and effectiveness of existing factuality-enhancement methods across benchmarks. No prior paper directly investigates the stability and consistency of factuality improvements across metrics and methods.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves re-evaluating a range of factuality-enhancement methods (contrastive-decoding methods like DoLa/CD/ICD and representation-editing methods like ITI/TruthX) on standard factuality benchmarks, comparing against an unmodified decoding baseline. Paper [13] introduces ITI, and paper [11] introduces TruthX, both of which are factuality-enhancement methods. Paper [21] empirically compares contrastive decoding methods (CD and CS) for open-ended text generation. These papers collectively cover the mechanism, as they involve the same technical primitives (contrastive decoding and representation editing) and benchmark-based comparisons, even if applied to different datasets or settings.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design uses TruthfulQA and FACTScore with LLAMA2-7B/13B-CHAT, measuring improvements and declines relative to baseline. Paper [13] evaluates ITI on TruthfulQA, and paper [11] evaluates TruthX on TruthfulQA. Paper [21] uses benchmarks to compare decoding methods, and paper [15] introduces HaluEval, a large-scale hallucination evaluation benchmark. These prior papers collectively cover the evaluation design, as they use similar benchmark families (TruthfulQA, FACTScore, or other factuality-related metrics) and validation setups. The specific choice of LLAMA2 models and metrics does not constitute a new evaluation design.

### Domain
The domain is LLM factuality/hallucination mitigation. Papers [5], [6], [8], [9], [13], [11], and others address hallucination mitigation or factuality improvement in LLMs, making this domain well-covered. While the contribution targets specific factuality-enhancement methods, this is a narrower instance within the broader domain of LLM factuality/hallucination mitigation, which is extensively studied in prior work.

Paper [7] also evaluates ICE methods, analyzing their impacts on token-wise distributions and accuracy. Both papers use the same evaluation design (ICE accuracy metrics and benchmarks like MQuAKE), making the evaluation covered.
